title: The runtime tree's top level sums to runtime
body:
The runtime tree had no branch for the work before the first mmseqs call, and nothing caught time spent outside the branches.

## Proposal

- `SerialTimed::Setup` covers everything from process start to the first mmseqs call. Its own enum `SetupTimed` has `QueryIndex`, `TargetIndex` and `PipelineBuild`. A `[misc.]` leaf takes argument validation, the mmseqs check and opening the output files.
- `build_pipeline` and the `--only-seed` early return move ahead of `seed()`, so the build sits inside setup. `build_pipeline` takes queries, targets, stats and args but not seeds, so nothing else moves.
- A root `[misc.]` makes runtime equal setup plus seeding plus alignment plus `[misc.]`.
- The progress lines "indexing ... done (Ns)" stay, and print the duration the timer records.
- The dead variant `ThreadedTimed::HmmBuild` goes.
close_reason: Landed in `ca4f33d`. The note on this issue has the details.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/415c993d
notes.text: Done on branch `runtime-tree`. `build_pipeline` takes `&Queries`, so `seed()` can borrow `pipeline.targets` and `pipeline.stats` afterwards. A helper `timed_step()` in `search.rs` replaced the four hand-written progress blocks and returns the duration. With `--only-seed` nail never builds the pipeline, so it records no setup and prints no tree, as before. Checked on the fixtures with `--seeds` and `--mmseqs-path /bin/true` in a release build. The debug build hits an assert that predates this change, filed as nail-7ab565.
